newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian shares mixed, big buyers seen sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Latvian shares mixed, big buyers seen sidelined.

text.p: Latvian shares were mixed on Tuesday and dealers said that big investors seemed to be holding out in an effort to bring some prices down.
Overall market volume was 122,000 lats and the Rietumu index slipped 0.24 percent to 190.13.
Rietumu said in a statement that its index was largely pulled down by the sharp drop in the Riga Transport Fleet (RTF), which eased 12.2 percent to 1.15 lats in trade of 14,500 lats.
"The price had to come down to attract buyers...it was a bit overpriced," said one dealer.

Dealers said that big investors appeared to be waiting for prices to ease further and that small investors seemed to be rising to the bait and attempting to shed their shares, boosting the supply and pushing down the prices of some stocks.
"When prices start to fall a bit, small investors get nervous," said one dealer.
Elsewhere on the official list, the short-term outlook was not so bleak. Unibanka extended its recent gains, rising to 3.50 lats from 3.40 lats in relatively high trade of 40,000 lats.
The Kaija fish cannery also gained, rising to 2.25 lats from 2.22 lats in trade of 16,900 lats, while the Riga Shipyard held steady at 1.38 lats in trade of 8,100 lats.
On the secondary list, the Daugavpils Chain factory was the most active stock in trade of 15,300 lats as it eased to 2.27 lats from 2.30 lats.
